label: Coffee at a café
notes: Specialty cafés in central Tokyo. Convenience-store coffee is ¥120-180.

label: 500ml water (konbini)
notes: Tap water is safe to drink; refill stations are growing.

label: Milk (1 L, supermarket)
notes: Full-fat cow's milk at Life, Maruetsu, or Seiyu. Brand-name organic ~¥400.

label: Bread (loaf, 5 slices)
notes: Classic shokupan — thick, soft, slightly sweet. Artisan bakeries charge ¥400-700.

label: Eggs (10 pack)
notes: Sold in packs of 10, not 12. Brown-shell free-range adds ¥80-150.

label: Konbini sandwich (egg or tuna)
notes: 7-Eleven's tamago sando is a meal-replacement staple — shockingly good for the price.

label: McDonald's Big Mac meal
notes: Big Mac ¥480 on its own; meal (fries + drink) ¥750. A standard comparison point worldwide.

label: KFC 2-piece combo
notes: Original Recipe chicken with fries + drink. KFC is the de-facto Christmas dinner in Japan.

label: Medium pizza delivery (Domino's / Pizza Hut)
notes: M-size margherita delivered. Takeout via half-price coupons ~¥1,400.

label: Casual meal (ramen, gyudon)
notes: Typical chain or independent shop, no drink.

label: Mid-range restaurant dinner
notes: Per person, one drink. Reservations often needed on weekends.

label: Beer at a pub/izakaya
notes: ½ pint / medium draft. Convenience-store cans: ¥220-350.

label: Bottle of wine (supermarket)
notes: Decent entry-level Chilean/Italian/Japanese red or white at a large supermarket.

label: Metro single ride
notes: Base fare; distance-based. Use Suica/Pasmo IC card to tap.

label: Taxi base fare
notes: First 1.096 km; then ¥100 per 255 m. Surcharge 22:00-05:00.

label: Taxi per extra km
notes: Approximate. Tolls not included.

label: Paracetamol / painkiller (24 tablets)
notes: Pharmacy only — no supermarkets. Tylenol A (Japanese Panadol equivalent). Bring your preferred brand if possible.

label: Sunscreen (SPF 50+, 50 g)
notes: Anessa, Biore UV — both world-class Japanese formulas. Widely exported but always cheaper at source.

label: Toothpaste (Colgate / local brand)
notes: Most toothpaste in Japan has very low fluoride (under 1000 ppm) by regulation. Bring your own if you need higher.

label: Cinema ticket (standard adult)
notes: Toho or United. Many chains drop to ¥1,300 on the 1st of each month ('Cinema Day').

label: Tourist SIM / eSIM (7 days)
notes: Varies by provider; eSIM often cheaper than physical SIM.

label: Tourist SIM / eSIM (30 days)
notes: Unlimited data plans from Airalo, Holafly, Ubigi and local telcos.

label: Coin locker (medium, day)
notes: At major stations. Ecbo Cloak starts around ¥500 for a backpack.

label: Museum entry (average)
notes: Major museums; smaller galleries often free or ¥500-800.

label: Gym day pass
notes: Anytime Fitness, Gold's, Tipness. Hotel gym use is often included with the room.

label: Haircut (men's, no wash)
notes: QB House — 10-minute cut, ¥1,200 fixed. Salons are ¥4,000-8,000.
